My suggestion is don't just try to memorize the material but try to really understand what the purpose of each step of each equation is. Also, try to study with someone who really knows the material well. They'll really help you improve the way you study and fine tune your mind to be more perceptive with every math problem. This got me through from calc 1 to diffeq

You're not approaching the subject the right way. You need to find a completely new way to think about the material. What you have been doing is not working, and it reflects in your grade. It's time to change something. Analyze how you have been learning the material, and look for a new way to learn.

You need to practice. Review and truly understand the material each week. Be part of a study group, if you're lucky, you'll know someone that reinforces their knowledge by teaching. Even if you just check out khan academy online, you need to switch how you are approaching the subject.

When I took Calculus 2 the thing that really made Calculus "click" was having my fundamentals down. Knowing a lot of basic trigonometry and knowing how two-dimensional functions behaved helped me go a long way.

The summer before you take a math course it may be worth doing a comprehensive review. Start with Khan academy and go through there calc. lessons as well as some of their pre-calc as it pertains to trig. Once you can handle that then you can go ahead and try some of the free MIT course material they have available. This will give you a head start and the pace might not seem as grueling.
